parts.problem_md:
Consider the logic expression:

**Z** = (**R** OR NOT **T**) XOR (NOT **S** AND** T**)

**Draw **a logic circuit for this logic expression.

Each logic gate must have a maximum of **two **inputs.

**Do not** simplify this logic expression.

![Rectangle with points R, S, and T on the left side and point Z on the right side, all marked outside the rectangle.](assets/001-rectangle-with-points-r-s-and-t-on-the-left-side.png)
parts.solution_md:
![Logic circuit diagram with NOT, OR, and AND gates, labelled inputs R, S, T, and output Z. Connections illustrate logic flow among the gates.](assets/002-logic-circuit-diagram-with-not-or-and-and-gates-.png)

- **Each **correct gate, with the correct input(s) as shown **[1 mark]**

parts.problem_md:
**Extract:**

- Accept a correct expression without the "P =" label (e.g. "(A AND B) OR NOT C") for full marks.
- Accept symbol notation (^ for AND, V for OR, \u00acC or NOT C) interchangeably.

**Write **the **Boolean expression **represented by the logic diagram below:

![Logic circuit diagram featuring an AND gate with inputs A and B, an OR gate outputting P, and a NOT gate with input C. Lines connect gates to the OR gate.](assets/003-logic-circuit-diagram-featuring-an-and-gate-with.png)
parts.solution_md:
The Boolean expression for the logic diagram can be expressed as:

- `P = (A AND B) OR (NOT C)` **OR  **`P = (A ^ B) V (¬C)`
- `(A AND B)` **[1 mark]**
- `(NOT C)` **[1 mark]**
- `(A AND B) OR (NOT C)` **[1 mark]**

> **[exam-tip]**
> Use parentheses to group each gate's output so the operator precedence is unambiguous
> 
> Match each gate exactly — an OR gate is an inclusive OR, not XOR
